# National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF): Official Methodology & Parameter Reference

**Source Authority:** Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India
**Applicability:** NIRF India Rankings (2017–2025 Editions)
**Document Purpose:** Grounded reference manual for NIRF parameters, sub-parameters, formulas, weightage structures, and ranking methodology.

---
section_title: National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF): Official Methodology & Parameter Reference
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
## 1. Overview of the Ranking Framework

The National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) was approved by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD, now Ministry of Education) in September 2015 to rank higher education institutions in India.

The framework outlines a methodology to rank institutions across various categories and subject domains:
- **General Categories:** Overall, Universities, Colleges, Research Institutions (introduced in 2021).
- **Domain-Specific Disciplines:** Engineering, Management, Pharmacy, Law, Medical, Architecture & Planning, Dental, Agriculture & Allied Sectors, Innovation, Skill University, Open University, State Public University.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
## 2. The Five Broad Ranking Parameters (Standard Schema)

Institutions in standard categories (Overall, Engineering, University, Management, Pharmacy, Colleges, etc.) are evaluated across five broad parameters, each evaluated out of 100 marks:

1. **Teaching, Learning & Resources (TLR)**
2. **Research and Professional Practice (RPC)**
3. **Graduation Outcomes (GO)**
4. **Outreach and Inclusivity (OI)**
5. **Perception (PR)**
section_title: 2. The Five Broad Ranking Parameters (Standard Schema)
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### Overall Weightage Distribution (Standard Category Example: Engineering & Overall)

| Parameter Code | Parameter Name | Engineering / Overall Weightage | University Weightage | Colleges Weightage | Management Weightage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TLR** | Teaching, Learning & Resources | 0.30 (30%) | 0.30 (30%) | 0.40 (40%) | 0.30 (30%) |
| **RPC** | Research and Professional Practice | 0.30 (30%) | 0.30 (30%) | 0.15 (15%) | 0.30 (30%) |
| **GO** | Graduation Outcomes | 0.20 (20%) | 0.20 (20%) | 0.25 (25%) | 0.20 (20%) |
| **OI** | Outreach and Inclusivity | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) |
| **PR** | Perception | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) | 0.10 (10%) |

The composite overall score is calculated as:
$$\text{Score} = w_{\text{TLR}} \times \text{TLR} + w_{\text{RPC}} \times \text{RPC} + w_{\text{GO}} \times \text{GO} + w_{\text{OI}} \times \text{OI} + w_{\text{PR}} \times \text{PR}$$

---

text: ## 3. Detailed Parameter Breakdown & Sub-Parameters
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 3.1. Teaching, Learning & Resources (TLR) — 100 Marks

TLR assesses the core academic inputs, human resources, faculty capacity, and physical/financial infrastructure dedicated to teaching and learning.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
#### Sub-Parameters of TLR:
1. **Student Strength including Doctoral Students (SS) — 20 Marks:**
 - Evaluates total sanctioned student intake across undergraduate (UG), postgraduate (PG), and enrolled PhD scholars.
 - Ratio of enrolled students compared to approved intake capacity.
 - Formula component: $SS = f(N_{\text{enrolled}}, N_{\text{approved}}) + f(N_{\text{phd}})$.

2. **Faculty-Student Ratio with Emphasis on Permanent Faculty (FSR) — 30 Marks:**
 - Evaluates the regular/permanent full-time faculty count against total student strength.
 - Target benchmark is typically 1:15 for Engineering/University, 1:10 for Medical, 1:20 for Colleges.
 - Part-time and visiting faculty have fractional or capped inclusion.

3. **Combined Metric for Faculty with PhD (or equivalent) and Experience (FQE) — 20 Marks:**
 - Assesses faculty academic qualifications (percentage of faculty holding a doctoral degree) and their teaching/industry experience depth ($FQ$ and $FE$).
 - High proportion of doctorate holders with >8-15 years experience maximizes this metric.

4. **Financial Resources and their Utilisation (FRU) — 30 Marks:**
 - Measures annual operational and capital expenditures per student over the preceding three financial years.
 - Operational expenses include laboratory consumables, library resources, maintenance of academic infrastructure, salaries of teaching and technical staff.
 - Capital expenses include creation of new buildings, specialized laboratories, and major equipment acquisitions.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 3.2. Research and Professional Practice (RPC) — 100 Marks

RPC assesses the scholarly output, research quality, intellectual property creation, and industry engagement of the institution.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
#### Sub-Parameters of RPC:
1. **Combined Metric for Publications (PU) — 35 Marks:**
 - Measures the total number of peer-reviewed research publications indexed in reputable citation databases (Web of Science and Scopus) over the preceding three calendar years.
 - Normalized relative to the number of faculty members.

2. **Combined Metric for Quality of Publications / Citations (QP) — 35 / 40 Marks:**
 - Measures the citation impact and quality of research output.
 - Evaluates total citations received in the preceding three years for publications published during the preceding three years.
 - Evaluates Top 25% percentile publications (highly cited papers / Q1 journals).
 - Includes $h$-index and citations per paper metrics.

3. **IPR and Patents: Published, Granted and Licensed (IPR) — 15 Marks:**
 - Measures patent activity over the preceding three years:
 - Patents published.
 - Patents granted.
 - Patents licensed and commercialized (technology transfer).

4. **Footprint of Projects and Professional Practice (FPPP) — 15 Marks:**
 - Evaluates sponsored research projects funding received from government and non-government agencies over three years.
 - Evaluates consultancy project earnings and executive development program earnings.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 3.3. Graduation Outcomes (GO) — 100 Marks

GO measures the real-world success of students completing their degrees from the institution.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
#### Sub-Parameters of GO:
1. **Metric for University Examinations (GUE) — 50–60 Marks:**
 - Percentage of students graduating in the minimum stipulated time without academic backlogs.
2. **Metric for Median Salary (GMS) — 25–40 Marks:**
 - Median annual salary of placed graduates over the previous three years as reported through verified placement records.
3. **Metric for Graduating Students Admitted to Top Higher Education / PhD (GPHD) — 15–20 Marks:**
 - Number of graduating students admitted to top national and international institutions for master's or doctoral programs, or the total number of PhD students graduated over the previous three years.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 3.4. Outreach and Inclusivity (OI) — 100 Marks

OI measures diversity, inclusivity, and equitable access across geographical, gender, and socio-economic lines.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
#### Sub-Parameters of OI:
1. **Percentage of Students from Other States / Countries (RD - Region Diversity) — 30 Marks:**
 - Measures geographical diversity of the student body: percentage of students enrolled from outside the home state and international students.
2. **Percentage of Women (WD - Women Diversity) — 30 Marks:**
 - Proportion of female students and female faculty members across all departments.
3. **Economically and Socially Challenged Students (ESC) — 20 Marks:**
 - Percentage of students receiving full or substantial tuition fee reimbursement from government or institutional scholarships.
4. **Facilities for Physically Challenged Students (PCS) — 20 Marks:**
 - Physical infrastructure for differently-abled students (wheelchair accessibility, ramps, lifts, specialized restrooms, assistive technologies).

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 3.5. Perception (PR) — 100 Marks

PR measures institutional reputation among academic peers, employers, and public stakeholders.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
#### Sub-Parameters of PR:
1. **Peer Perception: Academic Peers and Employers (PREMP) — 100 Marks:**
 - Survey-based assessment administered to academic peers (deans, professors, directors) and corporate recruiters/employers.
 - Objective is to assess academic standing, graduate capability, and overall brand prestige.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
## 4. Key Differences: TLR vs. RPC

A common point of inquiry is the fundamental distinction between TLR and RPC:

| Feature / Dimension | Teaching, Learning & Resources (TLR) | Research & Professional Practice (RPC) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Focus** | Educational inputs, internal resources, pedagogy | Research output, scholarly impact, external impact |
| **Key Inputs** | Enrolled student counts, faculty headcount, faculty qualifications | Indexed papers (Scopus/WoS), patents, grants |
| **Financial Factor** | Operational spending on labs, salaries, libraries | Sponsored research revenue and consultancy earnings |
| **Measurement Horizon**| Current academic year + 3-year expenditure average | Cumulative 3-year publication & citation window |
| **Institutional Role** | Assesses how well the institution teaches students | Assesses how actively the institution creates knowledge |

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
## 5. Research Specific Metric Schema (Introduced 2021)

Starting in 2021, NIRF introduced the dedicated **Research Institutions** category. Unlike the standard 5-parameter schema, this category uses a specialized schema:
1. **Research Scholarly Faculty & Capacity (`research_sfc`):** Focuses heavily on doctoral faculty, dedicated post-doctoral fellows, and research scholar density.
2. **Research Quantitative Output (`research_qnr`):** Focuses on publication volume, journal indexing depth, and faculty research productivity.
3. **Research Qualitative Metrics (`research_qlr`):** Focuses on citation impact, top-decile publications, high-impact journals, and collaborative international publications.
4. **Outreach & Inclusivity (`oi`):** Retained with focused weighting.
5. **Perception (`perception`):** Evaluates specialized research reputation.

---
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text: ## 6. Longitudinal Comparability & Cohort Boundaries
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 6.1. Expanding Ranking Depths
- In 2017, Management was ranked only to Rank 50, later expanding to Top 75 in 2020 and Top 100 in 2025.
- Engineering and Universities expanded from Top 100 to Top 200 (with ranks 101–200 placed in 50-rank bands).
- Colleges expanded from Top 100 to Top 200.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 6.2. Rank Bands (101–150 and 151–200)
- In NIRF, institutions ranked between 101–150 or 151–200 are reported in alphabetical or arbitrary order within bands.
- Numerical composite scores are deliberately withheld by NIRF for institutions in these bands.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
### 6.3. Annual Curve Normalization
- Composite scores and parameter scores are normalized annually relative to the highest-performing institution in that specific year and category.
- Consequently, an absolute TLR score of 72.5 in 2018 is not mathematically identical to 72.5 in 2024; cross-year tracking must account for cohort normalization.
source_reference: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India

text:
## 1. Executive Summary & The Problem of Ranking Drift

A foundational fallacy in longitudinal institutional ranking analysis is the naive assumption that a rank or score in one year is directly comparable to the same rank or score in another. In the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) across 2017–2025, rankings are subject to substantial structural evolution:

1. **Expanding Categories:** NIRF began in 2017 with 6 categories and expanded to 16 distinct categories by 2025.
2. **Expanding Ranking Depths:** Ranking lists have expanded dramatically (e.g., Pharmacy expanded from Top 50 to Top 75 to Top 100; Colleges expanded from Top 100 to Top 200).
3. **Scoring Normalization Shifts:** Composite scores are normalized within cohorts on an annual curve, meaning a score of 65.0 in 2017 reflects a different relative performance than 65.0 in 2025.
4. **Boundary Discontinuities:** Published ranks above 100 are grouped into unranked 50-rank bands (`101-150`, `151-200`) where composite scores are deliberately withheld.

To prevent invalid cross-year conclusions in Tableau, Streamlit, and Level 3 Hybrid RAG querying, this report details the structural rules operationalized in `comparability_rules_v3.csv`.

### Model A: Standard 5-Parameter Framework (98 Cohorts)
Applied to all standard academic categories (Overall, Engineering, Management, Pharmacy, Colleges, Architecture, Law, Medical, Dental, Research, Agriculture, State Public Universities):
1. **Teaching, Learning & Resources (TLR):** Weight ~30% (Colleges: 40%).
2. **Research and Professional Practice (RPC):** Weight ~30% (Colleges: 15%).
3. **Graduation Outcomes (GO):** Weight ~20% (Colleges: 25%).

### Model B: Innovation Framework (3 Cohorts: 2023–2025)
Formerly ARIIA (Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements), incorporated into NIRF in 2023. Evaluates patents granted, spin-offs, incubation infrastructure, and technology transfer revenue. Scores are **not** structurally comparable to Model A parameter scores.

## 4. Operational Guidelines for Dashboards & Querying

To ensure defensible analytical implementations:
source_reference: Senior Statistical Data Scientist & Academic Ranking Auditor

text:
### For Level 1: Tableau Dashboards
- **Trend Lines:** Do not draw uninterrupted time-series trend lines for categories across years prior to their official inception (e.g. Law cannot be charted before 2018; Dental before 2020).
- **Score Color Gradients:** Filter on `has_parameter_scores = True` when rendering heatmap visuals, as banded institutions (`rank_band in ['101-150', '151-200']`) have null scores and must be visually rendered with a neutral "Banded / Unscored" gray color.
source_reference: Senior Statistical Data Scientist & Academic Ranking Auditor

text:
### For Level 2: Streamlit Analytical Applications
- **Cohort Selector:** Use `comparability_rules_v3.csv` to dynamically populate available categories per year. If a user selects 2017 and attempts to filter by "Dental", display an informative alert: `"Dental ranking category was introduced in 2020"`.
- **Rank Velocity:** When calculating year-over-year rank delta (`rank_t - rank_{t-1}`), verify that both years are within numeric rank boundaries (ranks 1 to 100). Do not calculate numerical deltas for institutions transitioning into or out of unranked bands.
source_reference: Senior Statistical Data Scientist & Academic Ranking Auditor

text:
### For Level 3: Natural Language Assistant (Hybrid RAG)
- **Prompt Guardrail:** When answering questions such as *"How did IIT Madras perform in Innovation in 2020?"*, the LLM assistant must respond that the Innovation category was introduced in 2023.
- **Score Invariance Guardrail:** Prevent the LLM from comparing raw composite scores across different years (e.g., claiming an institution "declined" because its score dropped from 82.1 in 2021 to 80.5 in 2022, even if its rank improved from #4 to #3).

text:
## 1. Executive Summary & Audit Mandate

In multi-year institutional ranking datasets, identifier drift, institutional mergers, collegiate status elevations (to Deemed/State Unitary Universities), and data-entry variances across NIRF reporting cycles introduce substantial entity-resolution risks.

In Stage 3 (`V3`), we audited all 23 institutional identity transformations executed by `cleaning_script_v3.py`. Every transformation was evaluated against:
1. All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) unique institutional identifiers.
2. Official Acts of Parliament and State Legislatures establishing or renaming universities.
3. Ministry of Education (MoE) NIRF Data Capture System (DCS) sub-reports and official ranking PDFs.
4. Physical municipal locations and historical establishment dates.

**Core Principle:** Identity transformations are executed **only** when supported by incontrovertible statutory or institutional evidence. If identity cannot be proven beyond reasonable doubt, records are kept separate and flagged for manual DCS verification.

### A. Holy Cross College Disambiguation: Tiruchirappalli vs. Kanyakumari (Nagercoil)
- **The Challenge:** Two autonomous women's colleges operate under the historical title "Holy Cross College" in Tamil Nadu. The raw dataset contained an inconsistent UID assignment where a Tiruchirappalli entry in 2017 carried `C-35787`, while subsequent years carried `C-41223`.
- **Investigative Findings:**
 1. *Holy Cross College (Autonomous), Tiruchirappalli:* Established in 1923, affiliated with Bharathidasan University. AISHE Code: `C-41223`. NIRF IDs: `IR-C-C-41223`, `COL-1335`. Located in Teppakulam, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu.
 2. *Holy Cross College, Nagercoil (Kanyakumari):* Established in 1965, affiliated with Manonmaniam Sundaranar University. AISHE Code: `C-41124`. Located in Roch Nagar, Nagercoil, Kanyakumari District, Tamil Nadu.
- **Resolution in V3:**
 - Row-level condition: `(year == 2017) & (category == 'Colleges') & (institute_id == 'COL-1335') & (city_std == 'Tiruchirappalli')`.
 - Transformation: `C-35787` → `C-41223`.
 - Evidence: AISHE Master Directory 2021-22, NIRF 2017 College Ranking List PDF (Row 26), and Bharathidasan University affiliation list.
 - Confidence: **High (Definitive Statutory Match)**.

### B. St. Joseph's College Disambiguation: Devagiri (Calicut) vs. Irinjalakuda (Thrissur)
- **The Challenge:** Two premier autonomous colleges in Kerala named "St. Joseph's College" were assigned generic or colliding temporary NIRF identifiers (`I-1323` and `I-1322`) in the 2017 raw submission cycle.
- **Investigative Findings:**
 1. *St. Joseph's College (Autonomous), Devagiri, Calicut (Kozhikode):* Established in 1956, affiliated with University of Calicut. AISHE Code: `C-8010`. Located in Devagiri, Kozhikode, Kerala.
 2. *St. Joseph's College, Irinjalakuda, Thrissur:* Established in 1964, affiliated with University of Calicut. AISHE Code: `C-8106`. Located in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur, Kerala.
- **Resolution in V3:**
 - Devagiri: `(year == 2017) & (category == 'Colleges') & (city_std in ['Calicut', 'Kozhikode'])` → Transformed `I-1323` → `C-8010`.
 - Irinjalakuda: `(year == 2017) & (category == 'Colleges') & (city_std in ['Irinjalakuda', 'Thrissur'])` → Transformed `I-1323` / `I-1322` → `C-8106`.
 - Evidence: NIRF 2017 College Rankings Table (Devagiri ranked at #33; Irinjalakuda ranked at #42); University of Calicut College Directory.
 - Confidence: **High (Definitive Geographic & Collegiate Disambiguation)**.

### C. COEP: College of Engineering Pune (Collegiate Affiliation to Unitary State University)
- **The Challenge:** College of Engineering Pune appeared in 2017–2021 under AISHE college code `C-41593` (affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University), and in 2022–2025 under university code `U-1257` (COEP Technological University).
- **Investigative Findings:**
 - Established in 1854, COEP is the third oldest engineering college in Asia.
 - By the enactment of the *Maharashtra Act No. XXXV of 2022* (The COEP Technological University Act, 2022, published in Maharashtra Government Gazette on June 22, 2022), the Maharashtra State Legislature elevated the institute to a Unitary State Public University (`U-1257`).
- **Resolution in V3:**
 - Pre-2022 records (`C-41593`) are harmonized to canonical UID `U-1257` for longitudinal multi-year time-series continuity, while `institution_uid_raw` preserves `C-41593`.
 - Standardized Name: *COEP Technological University*.
 - Evidence: Maharashtra Govt Gazette Extraordinary Part VIII, June 22, 2022; AISHE University Code `U-1257`.
 - Confidence: **High (Statutory University Succession)**.

### D. Bharati Vidyapeeth: Poona College of Pharmacy (Constituent Deemed Unit)
- **The Challenge:** In Pharmacy 2017, the institute was listed under `C-41309`, while in 2018–2025 it appeared under `C-35417` / `U-0300` (Bharati Vidyapeeth Deemed to be University, Erandwane, Pune).
- **Investigative Findings:**
 - Poona College of Pharmacy was established in 1981 by Bharati Vidyapeeth. It became a constituent college of Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed to be University) under UGC Act 1956 Section 3 notification.
 - AISHE directory lists Poona College of Pharmacy under constituent code `C-35417`.
- **Resolution in V3:**
 - 2017 Pharmacy row with `C-41309` transformed to canonical `C-35417`.
 - Standardized Name: *Poona College of Pharmacy, Bharati Vidyapeeth*.
 - Evidence: MHRD Notification F.9-15/95-U.3 dated April 26, 1996; AISHE Portal Institution Directory.
 - Confidence: **High (Constituent Unit Harmonization)**.

### E. New Delhi Institute of Management (NDIM): Standalone Autonomous B-School
- **The Challenge:** In 2017 Management, NDIM appeared under `C-32887`, whereas subsequent NIRF editions listed it under standalone institute code `S-78`.
- **Investigative Findings:**
 - NDIM is an AICTE-approved standalone PGDM management institute established in 1992 in Tughlakabad Institutional Area, New Delhi.

- **Resolution in V3:**
 - 2017 Management row: `C-32887` → `S-78`.
 - Standardized Name: *New Delhi Institute of Management*.
 - Evidence: AICTE Approval Letters (File No. 740-89-009/PG/DM); AISHE Standalone Registry `S-78`.
 - Confidence: **High (Regulatory Registry Normalization)**.
